about: A synthetic questions graph for measuring whether a plain-English question finds the question it means (REM-998). Released under CC0-1.0. Fifty-six polar questions across unrelated fields, with distractors that share words with the reproduction question (valid, memory, time, method, agent) but not its meaning. Each question is answered by one to three invented claims with a stance. Written by an agent (Claude) on 19 October 2026 without reading the search code it tests.

questions.text: Should an agent's memory record when each fact became true, and not only when it was written down?

answers.claim: Storing the time a fact was written is enough for an assistant to answer questions about the past.
An assistant that keeps only write time answers 'where did she live in March' from whatever it heard last.
On the changing-facts benchmark, keeping the time each fact held lifted historical answers from 12% to 75%.

questions.text: Should an AI assistant forget what a user told it after a fixed number of days?

answers.claim: Fixed expiry removes facts a user still relies on.

questions.text: When two remembered facts about a user disagree, should the newer one simply replace the older?

answers.claim: Replacing the older fact loses the record that the user's situation changed.

questions.text: Is a vector store on its own enough to give an assistant a useful long-term memory?

answers.claim: Similarity search cannot say which of two similar facts is current.

questions.text: Is a clinical method that was validated in one hospital valid in another hospital?

answers.claim: Diagnostic accuracy measured at one site often drops at a second site with a different patient mix.

questions.text: Do validated survey methods stay valid when a questionnaire is translated?

answers.claim: Translated scales need their own validation before scores are compared.

questions.text: Is a passport valid for travel in its final six months?

answers.claim: Many countries refuse entry when a passport has fewer than six months left.

questions.text: Does a night of sleep strengthen human memory of what was learned that day?

answers.claim: Recall improves after sleep compared with an equal waking interval.

questions.text: Does adding more RAM make an ordinary laptop noticeably faster?

answers.claim: Beyond the working set, extra memory changes little for everyday tasks.

questions.text: Does working from home save people time overall?

answers.claim: Time saved on commuting is partly spent on extra working hours.

questions.text: Should a country stay on summer time all year round?

answers.claim: Permanent summer time leaves winter mornings dark for longer.

questions.text: Should travel agents charge a fee for booking flights?

answers.claim: Booking fees cover advice that airlines do not give.

questions.text: Do phonics methods teach young children to read better than whole-word methods?

answers.claim: Systematic phonics improves early decoding in controlled trials.

questions.text: Should a small analytics team move its warehouse off Postgres?

answers.claim: An embedded column store answers the team's aggregates faster on one machine.

questions.text: Does adding an index always make a database query faster?

answers.claim: An index slows writes and is ignored when a query reads most of a table.

questions.text: Should a team squash every pull request into a single commit?

answers.claim: Squashing loses the steps a reviewer could have bisected.

questions.text: Does lowering a language model's temperature make its answers more accurate?

answers.claim: Lower temperature makes answers repeatable, not more often right.

questions.text: Do smaller chunks always improve retrieval for question answering?

answers.claim: Very small chunks separate an answer from the context that makes it one.

questions.text: Does drafting with an AI weaken a writer's own judgement?

answers.claim: Writers who choose among suggestions keep their sense of authorship.

questions.text: Does homework improve results for primary school children?

answers.claim: The effect of homework is small before secondary school.

questions.text: Does a four-day working week keep output steady?

answers.claim: Firms in the trial reported stable revenue over six months.

questions.text: Does raising the minimum wage reduce employment among young workers?

answers.claim: Moderate increases showed little effect on teen employment.

questions.text: Does rent control reduce the supply of rental housing?

answers.claim: Landlords converted controlled units to owner-occupied housing.

questions.text: Does a carbon tax cut emissions without slowing growth?

answers.claim: Provinces with a carbon tax cut emissions while output grew.

questions.text: Should a country build new nuclear power stations to meet climate targets?

answers.claim: New plants take longer to build than the targets allow.

questions.text: Do electric car batteries usually last as long as the car?

answers.claim: Most packs keep over 80% of capacity after 200,000 km.

questions.text: Do heat pumps work in very cold winters?

answers.claim: Cold-climate heat pumps keep working well below freezing.

questions.text: Is drinking three cups of coffee a day bad for the heart?

answers.claim: Moderate coffee drinking is not linked to higher heart risk.

questions.text: Does intermittent fasting lead to more weight loss than ordinary dieting?

answers.claim: Trials find similar weight loss when calories are matched.

questions.text: Do vitamin D supplements prevent colds?

answers.claim: The benefit appears mainly in people who were deficient.

questions.text: Does looking at a phone before bed make it harder to fall asleep?

answers.claim: Evening screen use is linked to later sleep onset in teenagers.

questions.text: Does listening to music while studying hurt concentration?

answers.claim: Music with lyrics lowers reading comprehension.

questions.text: Does growing up bilingual delay a child's speech?

answers.claim: Bilingual children reach milestones within the normal range.

questions.text: Do open-plan offices increase face-to-face collaboration?

answers.claim: Face-to-face contact fell after two firms moved to open plan.

questions.text: Do daily stand-up meetings make software teams deliver faster?

answers.claim: Teams reported fewer blocked tasks, not faster delivery.

questions.text: Should a startup begin with microservices rather than a single application?

answers.claim: Early services multiply deployment work before the boundaries are known.

questions.text: Do static types reduce the number of bugs in production code?

answers.claim: Type checking catches a measurable share of bugs found in public repositories.

questions.text: Does mandatory code review catch most defects before release?

answers.claim: Review finds design problems more often than defects.

questions.text: Should an AI agent be allowed to run shell commands without asking first?

answers.claim: Unattended commands caused most of the destructive incidents reported.

questions.text: Do AI agents finish long tasks better when they write a plan first?

answers.claim: Agents that wrote a plan completed more multi-step tasks.

questions.text: Should a workflow engine forbid loops in its definitions?

answers.claim: A bounded repeat keeps a run finite and still allows retries.

questions.text: Should a failed booking undo the steps that already succeeded?

answers.claim: Compensation in reverse order leaves no half-made booking.

questions.text: Should access rules live in the database rather than in application code?

answers.claim: Row policies apply to every client, including the ones nobody reviewed.

questions.text: Is a database backup worth anything if nobody has tried restoring it?

answers.claim: Untested backups failed to restore in a third of reported outages.

questions.text: Should history be taught by dates or by themes?

answers.claim: Pupils taught by theme still need a timeline to place events.

questions.text: Should a newspaper archive show when an article was corrected?

answers.claim: A silent correction leaves readers unable to tell what was printed.

questions.text: Is an eyewitness's memory of a crime reliable months later?

answers.claim: Confidence grows while accuracy falls with each retelling.

questions.text: Does taking photos of an event make people remember it worse?

answers.claim: Visitors who photographed objects recalled fewer details of them.

questions.text: Has computer chess made human players stronger?

answers.claim: Average ratings of young players rose after engines became common.

questions.text: Can ground deformation predict a volcanic eruption days in advance?

answers.claim: Inflation preceded several eruptions but also occurred without one.

questions.text: Are neonicotinoid pesticides the main cause of bee decline?

answers.claim: Habitat loss and disease contribute as much as pesticides.

questions.text: Does planting trees on grassland help biodiversity?

answers.claim: Planting on species-rich grassland replaced a habitat rather than adding one.

questions.text: Should retirees keep most of their savings in shares?

answers.claim: A long retirement needs growth that cash cannot provide.

questions.text: Do index funds beat actively managed funds over twenty years?

answers.claim: Most active funds trailed their benchmark over two decades.

questions.text: Can a UK retail investor buy American-listed ETFs?

answers.claim: Brokers refuse US ETFs that publish no key information document.

questions.text: Do language models understand the meaning of the words they produce?

answers.claim: Models track relations between words without access to what they refer to.
